Former Synagogue in Sandhausen

Former Synagogue · Sandhausen, Germany

The building at Hauptstraße 115 in Sandhausen was constructed in 1755-57 as a Reformed church. In 1867 the local Jewish community purchased it for 2,000 gulden and converted it into a synagogue. During the November 1938 pogrom its interior was destroyed and the building was subsequently used for storage. Post-war plans to demolish it were abandoned after protests from the Jewish community in Heidelberg and heritage authorities. Following renovation from 1960 to 1962, the building reopened in May 1962 as a public library and meeting place, a use that continues today alongside cultural events. A memorial stone beside the building has commemorated the Jewish community since 1961.
